name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')
principle: The product builds all or part of a command with externally influenced input and fails to neutralize command special elements. The downstream command language can treat attacker data as syntax, delimiters, options, or a new command.
detection_signals: C/C++ system(cmd) or popen(cmd, ...) where cmd contains argv, getenv, socket, file, request, or config data
C/C++ execl/execle/execv/execve with "/bin/sh", "sh", "-c" or "cmd.exe", "/C" and user-built command text
Java Runtime.getRuntime().exec(String) where the string is concatenated with request, args, env, file, socket, or config data
Java ProcessBuilder("sh", "-c", userBuiltCmd) or ProcessBuilder("cmd.exe", "/C", userBuiltCmd)
string concatenation into protocol command text such as "USER " + input, "RCPT TO:" + input, or "SITE " + input followed by socket.write/send
user input concatenated into expression command text passed to ExpressionFactory.createValueExpression, SpELParser.parseExpression, MVEL.eval, or eval
blacklist validation removes only one delimiter such as ';' while allowing '|', '&', '&&', '||', '`', '$()', newline, or leading '-'
negative_signals: command operation selected from fixed enum/map and no raw user string is appended to command syntax
C/C++ execve(fixedPath, argvArray, envp) with no shell wrapper and validated argv elements
Java ProcessBuilder(List<String>) with fixed executable, separate arguments, no shell wrapper, and allowlisted argument values
anchored allowlist regex with length limit and rejection of command delimiters and dangerous leading '-'
library API replaces command execution, such as java.nio.file.Files, libarchive, DNS client API, or LDAP/SQL parameter API
expression or protocol API uses variables, bindings, or parameter objects instead of concatenated command text
false_defense_traps: denylist removes ';' but leaves '&&', '||', '|', '`', '$()', newline, or encoded delimiters
regex like ^[\w-]+$ allows leading '-' and enables option injection
Runtime.exec(String) treated as safe while the string invokes "sh -c" or "cmd.exe /C"
shell metacharacter escaping used while attacker-controlled options are still accepted without '--'
validation applied before URL decoding, environment expansion, glob expansion, or shell variable expansion
verification_focus: Can any externally influenced value become command syntax, delimiter, option, or command text for a downstream command language without strict allowlisting or structural separation?

consequence_chains.trigger: input reaches OS shell via system, popen, sh -c, or cmd.exe /C
input is passed as an argument but can contain delimiters or start with '-'
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker changes command options or command behavior

consequence_chains.trigger: input is concatenated into expression-language statement
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker evaluates unauthorized expressions or accesses objects

consequence_chains.trigger: input is used in an executable regular expression feature
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker executes unintended regex-level commands or code paths

patch_principle: Use library calls instead of external command interpreters where possible.
Construct commands statically; choose allowed operations from constants or an enum.
Pass dynamic values as structured argv arrays or parameter bindings, not concatenated command text.
Apply anchored allowlist validation for every dynamic field, including length and leading '-' rules.
Avoid shell wrappers such as sh -c and cmd.exe /C unless dynamic command text is removed.

minimal_examples.safe: if (!user.matches("^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,32}$")) throw new SecurityException(); socket.write(("SITE CHMOD " + user).getBytes());
